title: Agnuside from Vitex negundo L. Attenuates Hepatocellular Lipid Accumulation: Association with the AMPK/SREBP1/FASN/HMGCR/PPARalpha/UCP2 Signaling Network.
authors: Saikia, Abhipsha; Ahmed, Semim Akhtar; Saikia, Kangkon; Sarma, Pranamika; Basumatary, Devi; Mukherjee, Ashis K; Borah, Jagat Chandra; Bala, Asis
one_liner_zh: 研究植物提取物Agnuside对肝细胞脂质积累的调控作用，涉及分子对接与动力学模拟但对象为小分子-蛋白（HMGCR），非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Vitex negundo L. (VN) is a medicinal plant known for its anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective properties, commonly used as a vegetable in northeastern Indian communities. However, its role in treating nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is still underexplored. This study evaluates the therapeutic potential of VN and its bioactive compounds in reducing lipid accumulation in CC1 hepatocytes. A crude extract of VN and its n-butanol fraction (VNBU) were tested on palmitate-induced CC1 hepatocytes to evaluate lipid accumulation. Key compounds Agnuside, 5-hydroxy-3,6,7,3́,4́-pentamethoxyflavone, and Vitexilactone were isolated. Agnuside's effects on lipogenesis, cholesterol accumulation, and fatty acid oxidation were assessed using biochemical assays and Western blot analysis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to explore its interactions with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR). Agnuside treatment was associated with reduced lipid accumulation by modulating Adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), HMGCR, Sterol regulatory element-binding transcription factor 1 (SREBP1), Fatty acid synthase (FASN), Peroxisome Proliferator-activated receptors (PPARalpha), and uncoupling protein (UCP2), suggesting a favorable shift in lipid metabolism. Computational studies indicated that Agnuside binds stably to HMGCR, similar to statins. In summary, these findings suggest that VN and Agnuside exert protective effects in hepatocytes, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism markers. Further studies are needed to confirm the causal role of this signaling network.
abstract_zh: Vitex negundo L.（VN）是一种药用植物，以其抗炎和保肝特性而闻名，在印度东北部社区常作为蔬菜食用。然而，其在治疗非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）中的作用仍未得到充分探索。本研究评估了VN及其生物活性化合物在减少CC1肝细胞脂质积累方面的治疗潜力。对VN的粗提物及其正丁醇馏分（VNBU）在棕榈酸诱导的CC1肝细胞上进行了测试，以评估脂质积累情况。分离出关键化合物Agnuside、5-羟基-3,6,7,3́,4́-五甲氧基黄酮和Vitexilactone。通过生化分析和Western blot分析评估了Agnuside对脂肪生成、胆固醇积累和脂肪酸氧化的影响。进行了分子对接和动力学模拟，以探索其与3-羟基-3-甲基戊二酰辅酶A还原酶（HMGCR）的相互作用。Agnuside处理与脂质积累减少相关，通过调节腺苷单磷酸激活蛋白激酶（AMPK）、HMGCR、固醇调节元件结合转录因子1（SREBP1）、脂肪酸合酶（FASN）、过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARalpha）和解偶联蛋白（UCP2），提示脂质代谢发生有利转变。计算研究表明，Agnuside与HMGCR稳定结合，类似于他汀类药物。总之，这些发现表明VN和Agnuside在肝细胞中发挥保护作用，并伴随脂质代谢标志物的有利转变。需要进一步研究以确认这一信号网络的因果作用。
